documents.title: Student Guidance FAQ on Generative AI
documents.summary: Student FAQ saying Marquette has no university-wide AI policy and instructors decide. It advises students to follow syllabi, ask when unsure, disclose AI use, protect data, and frames AI use in Jesuit values and career preparation.
documents.stance_why: The FAQ says "Marquette does not have a university-wide policy" and "instructors decide on AI use for your courses", and lists assignment labels (no AI, limited, AI Friendly) that instructors may use; it sets no stance itself, so delegates with tiers.

units.why: The FAQ opens by stating the university's stance: "use AI tools responsibly and ethically". It is a framing principle for all students, so P56 (institution-wide framework), actor student, phase general, informs.
units.anchor: Marquette calls students to use AI tools responsibly and ethically.

units.why: "Review each course syllabus for rules on AI use" sends students to the syllabus as the source of the rule, so the course/instructor sets it (P04) rather than a general rule; it is addressed to students at the start of a course, a should.
units.anchor: Review each course syllabus for rules on AI use.

units.why: The FAQ lists labels instructors may attach to assignments: "No AI use allowed", "AI use limited", "AI Friendly". Named levels of use make this P05 (tiers), not P04, which is about who decides.
units.anchor: No AI use allowed (human brains only)
units.policy: Some instructors label assignments and assessments as no AI use allowed (human brains only), AI use limited (within guidelines), or AI Friendly (use responsibly and cite appropriately).

units.why: Students "uncertain about using AI" are pointed to a decision tree. This is the advice to check before using AI when unsure, so P10 fits better than P09 because it is addressed to students.
units.anchor: When assignment instructions are unclear or you are uncertain about using AI
units.frag_end: inappropriate uses of AI in your coursework.
units.policy: When assignment instructions are unclear or students are uncertain about using AI, they consult the May I Use AI for Classwork? decision tree to understand appropriate and inappropriate uses.

units.why: "Marquette does not have a university-wide policy" is a statement that no single rule exists and the decision lies lower down; it informs, and fits P04.
units.anchor: Marquette does not have a university-wide policy.

units.why: "instructors decide on AI use for your courses" hands the decision to instructors, the core of P04; it informs students who decides.
units.anchor: In general, instructors decide on AI use for your courses.

units.why: "The college or department offering your course may have its own AI guidelines" adds a further layer of local rule-setting. It is a delegation of rule-setting below the university, so P04 and not P11 (which is about non-carry-over between courses).
units.anchor: The college or department offering your course may have its own AI guidelines.

units.why: "If a tool creates or transforms your work, it's generative AI" defines what counts as AI for the policy, which is P61.
units.anchor: If a tool creates or transforms your work, it's generative AI.

units.why: The note that "word processors and spelling/grammar checkers" have "revamped into AI tools" extends the scope to AI embedded in ordinary software, matching P07 (AI built into tools) rather than P61 because the point is hidden embedded AI.
units.anchor: some long-standing software, such as word processors and spelling/grammar checkers, have revamped into AI tools

units.why: "If in doubt, check with your instructor" tells students to ask when unsure whether a tool counts as AI, so P10, should.
units.anchor: If in doubt, check with your instructor.

units.why: "If allowed by your instructor, AI can help you brainstorm ideas, summarize course content" permits conditional uses; brainstorming is the lead use, so P15 rather than P14 (summaries).
units.anchor: If allowed by your instructor, AI can help you brainstorm ideas, summarize course content
units.policy: If the instructor allows it, AI can help students brainstorm ideas, summarize course content and explore new perspectives.

units.why: "AI may short-circuit your learning, if it replaces critical thinking or problem solving" gives the learning reason for caution, P41.
units.anchor: AI may short-circuit your learning, if it replaces critical thinking or problem solving.

units.why: "AI can yield inaccurate or biased information" warns output may be wrong, which is P31 (verify output).
units.anchor: Keep in mind that AI can yield inaccurate or biased information.

units.why: "AI misuse may lead to academic integrity issues" links misuse to integrity processes, P36, as a statement of fact.
units.anchor: AI misuse may lead to academic integrity issues.

units.why: The self-check question "Is this use helping me learn or replacing the work I am meant to do?" asks students to stay the one doing the work, P32, as a should.
units.anchor: Is this use helping me learn or replacing the work I am meant to do?
units.policy: Before using AI, students consider whether the use helps them learn or replaces the work they are meant to do.

units.why: "Does the final work still reflect my own thinking, voice and values?" asks that submitted work remain the student's own, P29.
units.anchor: Does the final work still reflect my own thinking, voice and values?
units.policy: Before using AI, students consider whether the final work still reflects their own thinking, voice and values.

units.why: "would I feel comfortable explaining how I used AI to my instructor?" asks students to be ready to explain their use. It is nearest P30 (explain what you submit); P24 does not fit since no disclosure is required here.
units.anchor: would I feel comfortable explaining how I used AI to my instructor?
units.policy: Before using AI, students consider whether they would feel comfortable explaining to their instructor how they used AI.

units.why: "Struggle and effort are part of learning. AI should support learning, not skip it." states the rationale that AI should not skip the practice, P41, with a should.
units.anchor: AI should support learning, not skip it.

units.why: "Pause before you outsource work to AI, escaping the learning process" cautions against outsourcing practice, P41; it is advice, so should.
units.anchor: Pause before you outsource work to AI, escaping the learning process.

units.why: "Marquette recommends reaching out to campus resources" (instructor, writing center, library, ARC) directs stuck students to support before AI. No type covers support referral, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Marquette recommends reaching out to campus resources
units.policy: Marquette recommends that students feeling stuck, overwhelmed or behind reach out to campus resources (their instructor, Ott Writing Center, Raynor Library, Academic Resource Center) before turning to AI.
units.uncovered_note: Recommendation to use human campus support services (instructor, writing center, library, academic resource center) before consulting AI.

units.why: "Do not enter personal, confidential or sensitive information into public AI tools" is a data-protection prohibition, P50.
units.anchor: Do not enter personal, confidential or sensitive information into public AI tools.

units.why: "may lose control of your data" explains that public tools can reuse entered data; it supports the privacy rule, P50, as information.
units.anchor: may lose control of your data
units.policy: Students may lose control of their data when they enter it into a public AI tool, which could reuse it to answer questions asked by anyone else.

units.why: "Follow guidance from your instructor or faculty researcher on approved and supported AI tools" points students to vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: Follow guidance from your instructor or faculty researcher on approved and supported AI tools.

units.why: "not all AI platforms protect your data in the same way" warns that platforms differ in data protection, P50.
units.anchor: Remember that not all AI platforms protect your data in the same way.
units.frag_end: your data in the same way.

units.why: "Start with the AI Tool List, noting which tools are available to students" points students to a university list of available tools, P17 (sanctioned tools).
units.anchor: noting which tools are available to students
units.policy: Students start with the AI Tool List, noting which tools are available to them.

units.why: "Ask your instructor before using AI for your classwork" is the action when the syllabus is silent, P10 (ask first), distinct from the fallback rule below.
units.anchor: Ask your instructor before using AI for your classwork.

units.why: "Don't assume omission of AI from the syllabus means you can use AI" fixes the rule when the syllabus is silent, P06; it restricts use absent approval.
units.anchor: Don't assume omission of AI from the syllabus means you can use AI.

units.why: "Using AI (without instructor approval) is not individual work" ties unapproved AI to the Honor Code requirement to work individually, so it is misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Using AI (without instructor approval) is not individual work.

units.why: "submitting AI work as your own is plagiarism" classifies undisclosed AI work as plagiarism, handled under integrity processes, P36.
units.anchor: Yes, submitting AI work as your own is plagiarism.

units.why: The quoted misconduct policy defines plagiarism to include "lacking or unclear attribution of content developed with generative software", a definition of misuse, P36.
units.anchor: including lacking or unclear attribution of content developed with generative software

units.why: "disclose and attribute AI use" tells students to acknowledge AI use to avoid misconduct, P24.
units.anchor: To avoid academic misconduct, disclose and attribute AI use.

units.why: Students are "obliged to report any observed breaches" of the honor code, including AI plagiarism. No type covers a peer-reporting duty, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: to report any observed breaches of this honor code and academic honesty.
units.policy: Students are obliged to report observed breaches of the honor code and academic honesty; they may talk to the instructor or submit an Academic Misconduct Report Form, which has an anonymous option.
units.uncovered_note: Students' duty to report peers' AI-related academic misconduct, with anonymous reporting option.

units.why: "Your instructor specifies which citation style to use for attribution" leaves the form of AI attribution to instructors; it concerns how to cite AI, P24.
units.anchor: Your instructor specifies which citation style to use for attribution.

units.why: "learning how to use AI responsibly now prepares you to" collaborate, justify decisions and act with social responsibility: a professional-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: learning how to use AI responsibly now prepares you to
units.frag_start: At Marquette, learning how to use
units.policy: At Marquette, learning to use AI responsibly prepares students to collaborate effectively with technology, explain and justify their decisions, and use tools in ways that honor human dignity and social responsibility.

units.why: "follow each instructor's direction about AI in your course" repeats that the instructor decides and the student follows; P04, should.
units.anchor: follow each instructor's direction about AI in your course

units.why: "Using AI in ways not permitted by your instructor may violate Marquette's academic integrity policies" classes unpermitted use as an integrity violation, P36.
units.anchor: Using AI in ways not permitted by your instructor may violate

units.why: "AI will be part of many professions you enter after graduation" is a career rationale, P44.
units.anchor: AI will be part of many professions you enter after graduation.

units.why: "Employers expect not just technical skill but judgment, ethics and accountability" states what employers want, a professional-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: Employers expect not just technical skill but judgment, ethics and accountability.

units.why: "it is not a substitute for your thinking" says students remain the thinker, P32.
units.anchor: it is not a substitute for your thinking.

units.why: "Your instructors set expectations; when unsure, ask" repeats the ask-first advice in the takeaways, P10.
units.anchor: Your instructors set expectations; when unsure, ask.

units.why: "Reflect on how AI use affects your learning and integrity" asks for self-reflection; closest to P32 (student keeps charge of own learning). It is not a submitted reflection, so not P26.
units.anchor: Reflect on how AI use affects your learning and integrity.

units.why: "Use AI in ways that align with Marquette's values" states a general principle for use, P56.
units.anchor: Use AI in ways that align with Marquette
units.policy: Students use AI in ways that align with Marquette's values and their own growth.

units.why: "Jesuit values challenge students to approach AI with discernment" grounds the approach in the Catholic, Jesuit mission, a framework statement, P56.
units.anchor: Jesuit values challenge students to approach AI with discernment.

documents.title: AI, Generative and Emerging Technologies Support for the Classroom
documents.summary: CTL page telling instructors that Marquette has no unified AI policy in favor of instructional flexibility. It asks instructors to state expectations clearly and offers presentations, videos and help for learning about AI.
documents.stance_why: The page states "Marquette does not have a unified AI policy in favor of instructional flexibility" and asks instructors to articulate what they encourage, prohibit and find acceptable; the decision is delegated to instructors.

units.why: "Marquette does not have a unified AI policy in favor of instructional flexibility" says the university sets no policy and leaves the choice to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: Marquette does not have a unified AI policy in favor of instructional flexibility

units.why: "your college or department may have its own guidelines" notes a local layer of rules, P04.
units.anchor: your college or department may have its own guidelines

units.why: "students need and deserve clear articulations of what your expectations are" tells instructors to state their AI expectations; it addresses instructors before the term and corresponds to P09.
units.anchor: students need and deserve clear articulations of what your expectations are
units.policy: Instructors give students clear articulations of their expectations on AI (what they encourage, what they prohibit, what they find acceptable) and why.

units.why: "Recommended communication with students can be found below" offers recommended wording and visuals for syllabi; it suggests instructors communicate in the syllabus, P09, should.
units.anchor: Recommended communication with students can be found below.

units.why: The CTL "offers customized sessions on AI resources, responsible use, course design considerations" for departments, which supports faculty in learning about AI, P63.
units.anchor: offers customized sessions on AI resources, responsible use, course design considerations, and department-level discussions
units.frag_start: Interested in a conversation about AI

units.why: The video series shows "faculty and students reflecting on how they are both discerning and may be engaging AI", a faculty learning resource, P63.
units.anchor: features faculty and students reflecting on how they are both discerning
units.frag_end: Ignatian Pedagogy and our Jesuit mission.

units.why: The CTL and a librarian offer help with "how to design your assignments in light of it" and discussing AI with students, which is support for faculty, P63.
units.anchor: how to design your assignments in light of it
units.frag_start: For help learning more about AI
units.policy: The CTL and the Digital Scholarship Librarian help instructors learn about AI, discuss it with students, and design assignments in light of it.

documents.title: Academic Integrity
documents.summary: Provost academic-integrity page on reporting misconduct. Its AI content is brief: talk with students first, give specific examples when alleging unattributed generative-software use, and treat AI detectors as unreliable evidence.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no allow or ban rule for AI; its only AI statements concern how to report suspected unattributed use and the unreliability of "AI detectors", so the stance is delegates (rules sit elsewhere).

units.why: "We encourage all instructors to speak with their students about potential allegations before submission" asks instructors to talk with the student before escalating, P57.
units.anchor: speak with their students about potential allegations

units.why: "ensure that your report includes explicit rationales with specific examples" of suspected unattributed AI material sets an evidence expectation for reports. It is nearest P40 (evidence to identify misuse); P36 only classifies misconduct.
units.anchor: ensure that your report includes explicit rationales with specific examples
units.policy: If an allegation includes suspicion of unattributed use of generative software, the report includes explicit rationales with specific examples of the suspected unattributed material.

units.why: "AI detectors offer both false positives and false negatives" and their findings as evidence "are less reliable", so detectors should not be relied on alone, P39.
units.anchor: AI detectors" offer both false positives and false negatives
units.policy: AI detectors offer both false positives and false negatives, so their findings as evidence of misconduct are less reliable in the absence of other evidence.

units.why: The page lists "Resources Concerning Generative Software (Generative AI) in a Catholic and Ignatian Context" (papal documents and guidance), framing the university's approach to AI in its Catholic tradition, P56.
units.anchor: Resources Concerning Generative Software

notes: Responsible-use ITS PDF was screened exclude and not coded. Two UNCOVERED units (campus-resource referral; peer-reporting duty). No school/computing/course docs available for Marquette.
